hook.text: BCH codes were independently discovered by three mathematicians on three continents in 1959-1960. Great ideas converge.

buildup.text: BCH (Bose-Chaudhuri-Hocquenghem) codes are a family of cyclic codes with precise error-correcting guarantees.

discovery.text: For any desired number of correctable errors t, a BCH code exists with known length and redundancy.

twist.text: Reed-Solomon codes are actually a special subclass of BCH codes—operating on multi-bit symbols instead of single bits.

climax.text: BCH codes are used in flash memory (SSDs), satellite links, and DVB. Their algebraic structure makes decoding efficient.

punchline.text: Three discoverers. One family of powerful codes.

quiz.question: What is the relationship between Reed-Solomon and BCH codes?
options: Reed-Solomon codes are a special subclass of BCH codes
BCH codes are simpler than Reed-Solomon
